attempts.rationale: Robust baseline: unstable rankings + correlated errors favor trimming worst 20% of models to reduce influence of consistently bad performers while preserving diversity across correlation groups.
Baseline mean over all 19 models to compare against trimmed_mean; tests whether tail models hurt or help given unstable ranking

Median over all 19 models as a more extreme robust aggregator than trimmed_mean; tests whether ignoring all tail models (not just trimming 20%) helps under unstable ranking (tau=-0.092) and correlated errors (7 groups).

Test whether inverse-error weighting helps vs. robust unweighted combos given unstable ranking (tau=-0.092) and small relative spread (1.029); if it underperforms, the error differences are too noisy to exploit
DBA adjusts for directional bias; with strong trend and unstable ranking, directional optimization may outperform level-based robust combinations (trimmed_mean, median, mean) already tested
DBA on top-7 SMAPE pool (4 correlation groups) vs full 19-model pool; tests whether reducing redundancy helps DBA converge to a better blend given unstable ranking
Per-horizon top-k weighting to exploit horizon-specific model strengths given strong seasonality and unstable ranking; tests whether the best 3 models change along the 8-step horizon

Testing whether softmax weighting (more sensitive to error spread than inverse_error) better exploits cross-cluster complementarity in a series with strong seasonality and unstable ranking; DBA leads but weighted-softmax is a different kind of robust aggregation

Unstable ranking (tau=-0.092) suggests model performance shifts across windows; error_trend weights adapt to recent improvement rather than average error, testing whether recency matters for this strongly-trended series

Meta-model weights use cross-series patterns to weight models, which should be more stable than in-sample error weights given the unstable ranking (tau=-0.092). Tests whether external structural knowledge improves on the robust dba leader.
Per-horizon top-5 (smape) weighting: different models lead at different steps given unstable cross-window ranking; tests whether horizon-specific diversification beats the robust full-pool DBA leader
DBA on top-2 uncorrelated models (ARIMA rank1, ETS rank2) tests whether removing 17 weaker/correlated models helps the robust combination converge better than the full-pool DBA leader
